items.headline: Fed hikes rates 25bp to 3.75%-4.00% as oil-driven inflation persists, dot plot turns hawkish
items.summary: The FOMC raised the federal funds rate to 3.75%-4.00%, citing inflation pressure partly tied to the Iran-conflict oil spike. The September dot plot showed 16 of 18 officials expecting at least one more hike in 2026, with four seeing two more as possible.
items.actionable: This hawkish pivot (not a cut) is the root cause of the precious-metals reversal seen this week -- real yields and the dollar are rising, a structural headwind for the levered silver/miner book, while it's a tailwind for net-interest-margin at DBS/OCBC/UOB.

items.headline: Silver and gold miners post sharpest one-day reversal in months as the dollar surges on hawkish Fed speak
items.summary: SLV fell 4.23% to $58.16 and GDX fell 4.36% as Richmond Fed's Barkin said inflation risks 'outweigh' employment risks, pushing the Dollar Index to a 7-week high near 100.7-100.9. Silver miners AG (-6.25%) and HL (-3.99%) amplified the move after the metals' multi-day breakout stalled at resistance, triggering profit-taking and stop-loss selling.
items.actionable: This looks like a dollar/technical-driven pullback rather than a fundamentals break, but the levered silver/miner sleeve should expect continued volatility until the dollar and Fed-hike odds stabilize.

items.headline: WTI falls 2.58% to $92.15 on surprise EIA crude inventory build
items.summary: The EIA reported a surprise US crude stock build of +2.97M barrels versus a forecast -0.7M draw, sending WTI down 2.58% on Sept 23. The move is idiosyncratic to US inventory data rather than a reflection of the parallel Hormuz de-escalation diplomacy playing out at the UN this week.
items.actionable: An oversupply-driven pullback is modestly disinflationary for the broad consumer and a negative for energy-equity near-term momentum; the owner has no direct energy sleeve, so this is a watch-only item.

items.headline: Iran proposes region-wide ceasefire and phased Hormuz reopening at UN talks; two tankers hit Sept 21
items.summary: US and Iranian officials held Qatar/Pakistan/Egypt-mediated talks at the UN General Assembly, with Iran offering a ~60-day regional ceasefire and phased reopening of the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for an end to the US blockade. Two tankers were struck in the Strait on September 21, and a senior Iranian official said the strait could reopen within seven days if military pressure eases -- but Trump has ruled out lifting the blockade before Iran shows sufficient goodwill.
items.actionable: Any credible Hormuz de-escalation would remove the war-risk premium underpinning both oil and gold's safe-haven bid, adding to the metals reversal risk; watch for a formal ceasefire announcement as a bearish trigger for gold/silver and bullish for broader risk assets.

items.headline: Trump hosts Xi at White House for state visit; agenda covers trade, AI, Taiwan, Ukraine and Gaza
items.summary: President Trump and First Lady Melania Trump are hosting Xi Jinping and Peng Liyuan at the White House on September 24 for a formal state visit, including a State Arrival Ceremony. Analysts (CSIS, Atlantic Council) say expectations for major breakthroughs are low, with AI safeguards seen as the most likely area of cooperation, while trade, technology controls and Taiwan remain the core points of friction.
items.actionable: Low expectations mean any surprise on tech-export relief or rare-earth licensing would be a sharp positive catalyst for HK tech/semis and the rare-earth basket, while a breakdown or new tariff threat would hit 0700/0981/1810 and MP/Lynas via renewed export-control risk.

items.headline: MP Materials shares jump ~6-8% over two sessions on strong Q2 NdPr production growth despite analyst target cut
items.summary: MP Materials stock rose 5.99% on Sept 21 to $50.09 and a further 2.1% on Sept 22 after operating data showed Q2 revenue up 89% y/y to $108.5m, with NdPr production up 41% y/y (840 metric tons) and sales up 127% y/y. JPMorgan nonetheless cut its price target from $75 to $60 while keeping an Overweight rating.
items.actionable: Production momentum is real and outpaced the China export-control overhang into the Sept 23 pullback -- supportive for the rare-earth watchlist's core MP position, though the JPMorgan target cut flags valuation/margin caution worth tracking.

items.headline: Tencent jumps as much as 7% intraday on Meta's Muse AI-agent success, seen as read-through for WeChat's Xiaowei
items.summary: Tencent shares rallied on September 22 after Meta's AI agent app Muse topped the US App Store and lifted Meta shares 11%; investors read this as bullish for Tencent's own in-development WeChat AI agent, Xiaowei. Separately, Tencent's new AI image model is drawing comparisons with offerings from ByteDance and Alibaba.
items.actionable: The AI-agent narrative is becoming a real share-price driver for 0700 independent of the broader HK tech tape -- worth monitoring Xiaowei's actual WeChat rollout as the next catalyst for the position.

items.headline: Xiaomi buys back HK$48.9m of shares; CXMT to supply domestic LPDDR6 DRAM for new foldable flagship
items.summary: Xiaomi repurchased 1.8 million Class B shares for HK$48.9 million on September 22. Separately, China's top memory chipmaker CXMT will supply LPDDR6 DRAM for Xiaomi's upcoming flagship foldable phone (Xiaomi 18 Fold), reinforcing the domestic semiconductor substitution trend alongside SMIC's foundry role.
items.actionable: Continued buybacks plus deepening reliance on domestic chip suppliers (CXMT/SMIC) support the thesis that Xiaomi and SMIC are direct beneficiaries of China's tech self-sufficiency push, independent of the Trump-Xi summit outcome.

items.headline: Jefferies initiates Singapore banks with Buy on DBS/UOB, Hold on OCBC as STI holds near record highs
items.summary: Jefferies started coverage of Singapore banks on September 22, rating DBS and UOB Buy and OCBC Hold, citing scope for further earnings and dividend growth. The Straits Times Index has held near its record high (above 5,800, hit September 4), with DBS/UOB/OCBC together representing roughly 57% of index weight, and the September 16 Fed hike seen as a further net-interest-margin tailwind for the trio.
items.actionable: Fresh sell-side conviction plus a rate backdrop that widens bank margins supports staying long DBS/UOB within the SGX bank sleeve; OCBC's Hold rating suggests relatively less upside versus peers.

items.headline: Bitcoin trades near $84,300, still well below its October 2025 all-time high of $126,210
items.summary: Bitcoin traded in an $84,250-$84,500 range on September 24, up roughly 0.7% over 24 hours, with BTC dominance at about 61% of total crypto market cap and 24-hour volume near $47.2 billion. Price remains about a third below its October 6, 2025 record high.
items.actionable: Crypto is drifting sideways well off highs with no fresh catalyst identified -- low urgency for the portfolio's cash-deployment decisions relative to the metals and geopolitics moves above.
